resources.string: Unpack and run Debian packages on Android, no root required.
Environment is ready. Open the terminal or install a .deb package.
The root filesystem and every installed package will be deleted.
The package is unpacked inside the Linux container, never into the Android system.
Select a package to preview its metadata.
Small download, newest glibc, best compatibility with most .deb files.
Changing the distribution requires re-initializing the environment.

DebRun is an open source container runtime for Android. It bundles PRoot, a Debian/Ubuntu root filesystem and a terminal, so a .deb package can be unpacked and executed inside the app sandbox without root, without unlocking the bootloader and without touching the Android system partition.

How it works:
1. PRoot emulates chroot through ptrace, so an ordinary app can own a Linux filesystem tree.
2. A root filesystem is downloaded once, verified and extracted into the app's private storage.
3. .deb files are handed to dpkg inside that tree; missing dependencies are resolved by apt.
4. The bundled terminal (xterm.js) drives an interactive shell in the same tree.

Limitations: GUI (X11) programs need an X server and are not displayed yet; kernel modules, init systems and hardware device nodes are not available; 32-bit binaries on 64-bit devices are not supported.

Source code, licenses and issue tracker: the project is published on GitHub under the DebRun repository.

1. DebRun runs a full Linux userland on your device. Packages you install execute with the app's own permissions inside the sandbox; they cannot modify the Android system, but they can read and write the files you granted.

2. Install only .deb files you trust and from sources you trust. A package may contain any code and will run inside the container with your app's network and storage access. DebRun does not sandbox individual packages from each other.

3. Root filesystem images and Debian packages are downloaded from third-party mirrors. Availability, integrity and licensing of those files are the responsibility of their providers.
